ACCT-2754.title: FreeBSD Process Accounting Disabled
ACCT-2754.control_detail: Lynis Control ACCT-2754 verifies BSD process accounting daemon status to ensure historical command execution records are kept.
ACCT-2754.description: Process accounting is a method to track system resources, recording user activity, command executions, and CPU/memory utilization over time.
ACCT-2754.how_to_solve:
1. Add 'accounting_enable="YES"' to /etc/rc.conf.
2. Create accounting file: touch /var/account/acct
3. Start accounting service: /etc/rc.d/accounting start
ACCT-2754.business_impact: Lack of non-repudiation and inability to reconstruct past administrator actions during incident forensics.
ACCT-2754.remediation_cmd: echo 'accounting_enable="YES"' | sudo tee -a /etc/rc.conf && sudo service accounting start
ACCT-2754.rollback_note: Remove accounting_enable from /etc/rc.conf and stop the accounting service.

ACCT-9622.title: Linux Process Accounting (acct/psacct) Inactive
ACCT-9622.control_detail: Lynis Control ACCT-9622 audits the status of Linux process accounting (acct or psacct) which records every executed command with user and runtime metrics.
ACCT-9622.description: Process accounting logs all commands executed by all users on the Linux host into /var/log/account/pacct. Without process accounting, attackers can execute ephemeral commands without leaving standard shell history traces.
ACCT-9622.how_to_solve:
1. Install the process accounting package (psacct or acct).
2. Enable the systemd service.
3. Verify accounting is active using 'ac' or 'lastcomm'.
ACCT-9622.business_impact: Compromised forensics capability; unable to determine what commands an attacker executed during a security breach.
ACCT-9622.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y acct && sudo systemctl enable --now acct || (sudo yum install -y psacct && sudo systemctl enable --now psacct)

ACCT-9626.title: Sysstat System Accounting Data Inactive
ACCT-9626.control_detail: Lynis Control ACCT-9626 tests whether the sysstat package (sar, iostat) is collecting performance and resource accounting metrics.
ACCT-9626.description: Sysstat records continuous resource utilization trends (CPU, RAM, network, I/O) allowing baseline comparisons and identification of resource-draining malicious payloads or cryptocurrency miners.
ACCT-9626.how_to_solve:
1. Install sysstat package.
2. Set ENABLED="true" in /etc/default/sysstat.
3. Restart and enable sysstat service.
ACCT-9626.business_impact: Inability to detect sudden spikes in network or CPU utilization caused by botnets or cryptominers.
ACCT-9626.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y sysstat && sudo sed -i 's/ENABLED="false"/ENABLED="true"/' /etc/default/sysstat && sudo systemctl enable --now sysstat
ACCT-9626.rollback_note: Set ENABLED="false" in /etc/default/sysstat and stop service.

ACCT-9628.title: Linux Audit Framework Daemon (auditd) Inactive
ACCT-9628.control_detail: Lynis Control ACCT-9628 inspects the Linux kernel audit framework (auditd) service status.
ACCT-9628.description: Auditd monitors kernel-level system calls, tracking unauthorized file modifications, permission alterations, and execution of privileged binaries. When disabled, security monitoring cannot detect low-level system subversions.
ACCT-9628.how_to_solve:
1. Install auditd and audispd-plugins.
2. Enable and start auditd system service.
3. Load basic rule set in /etc/audit/rules.d/audit.rules.
ACCT-9628.business_impact: Fails compliance requirements for PCI-DSS, SOC 2, HIPAA, and CIS Benchmarks. Critical security events go unrecorded.
ACCT-9628.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y auditd audispd-plugins && sudo systemctl enable --now auditd

ACCT-9630.title: Empty Audit Daemon Ruleset Detected
ACCT-9630.control_detail: Lynis Control ACCT-9630 checks if auditd is running with an empty or non-configured ruleset.
ACCT-9630.description: An audit daemon running with zero rules will not record critical security events such as modifications to /etc/passwd, /etc/sudoers, or execution of setuid binaries.
ACCT-9630.how_to_solve:
1. Deploy baseline security rules to /etc/audit/rules.d/audit.rules.
2. Run augenrules --load to compile and load rules.
3. Verify active rules with 'auditctl -l'.
ACCT-9630.business_impact: False sense of security: audit daemon is active but capturing no meaningful security telemetry.
ACCT-9630.remediation_cmd: echo -e '-w /etc/passwd -p wa -k identity\n-w /etc/shadow -p wa -k identity\n-w /etc/sudoers -p wa -k actions' | sudo tee -a /etc/audit/rules.d/audit.rules && sudo augenrules --load
ACCT-9630.rollback_note: Remove custom rules from /etc/audit/rules.d/audit.rules and reload with augenrules --load.

ACCT-9632.title: Auditd Configuration File Undiscovered
ACCT-9632.control_detail: Lynis Control ACCT-9632 tests if the auditd configuration file (auditd.conf) is present in standard paths (/etc/audit/).
ACCT-9632.description: Missing or improperly placed auditd configuration file prevents the daemon from applying buffer sizes, log rotation parameters, and failure handling modes.
ACCT-9632.how_to_solve:
1. Locate or reinstall default auditd.conf file in /etc/audit/auditd.conf.
2. Ensure permissions are 640 root:root.
ACCT-9632.business_impact: Potential loss of audit logs due to unmanaged log rotation or daemon crash under high load.
ACCT-9632.remediation_cmd: sudo cp /usr/share/doc/auditd/examples/auditd.conf /etc/audit/auditd.conf 2>/dev/null || sudo apt install --reinstall -y auditd

ACCT-9636.title: Linux Command Audit Trail (Snoopy Logger) Missing
ACCT-9636.control_detail: Lynis Control ACCT-9636 checks if Snoopy logger or an equivalent LD_PRELOAD command auditor is deployed.
ACCT-9636.description: Snoopy is a lightweight library that logs all executed commands with authentic username, UID, PID, and timestamp directly to syslog, preventing log tampering by compromised shells.
ACCT-9636.how_to_solve:
1. Install snoopy package via package manager.
2. Enable in /etc/ld.so.preload.
3. Check /var/log/auth.log for command execution entries.
ACCT-9636.business_impact: Attackers clearing ~/.bash_history leave no secondary trace of executed commands.
ACCT-9636.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y snoopy && sudo snoopy-enable || true

PKGS-7392.title: Installed Software Packages with Known Vulnerabilities
PKGS-7392.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7392 queries the local package manager and vulnerability database to identify installed software packages with known security flaws (CVEs) and available vendor security patches.
PKGS-7392.description: Your system has installed applications and libraries with confirmed public security vulnerabilities (CVEs) that have official security patches available from your distribution repository.
PKGS-7392.how_to_solve:
1. Refresh package index repositories: sudo apt update
2. Perform a full security upgrade: sudo apt --with-new-pkgs upgrade -y
3. Remove obsolete orphaned packages: sudo apt autoremove -y
4. Enable automated unattended security upgrades to prevent recurring vulnerabilities.
PKGS-7392.business_impact: Unpatched vulnerabilities are the primary attack vector exploited by automated botnets, ransomware operators, and remote code execution frameworks.
PKGS-7392.remediation_cmd: sudo apt update && sudo apt --with-new-pkgs upgrade -y && sudo apt autoremove -y
PKGS-7392.rollback_note: Specific packages can be pinned with 'sudo apt-mark hold <pkg>'.

PKGS-7394.title: Outdated Software Packages with Known Security Advisories
PKGS-7394.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7394 interrogates the local package manager for unpatched packages with published security advisories.
PKGS-7394.description: Your system has installed applications and libraries with known public security vulnerabilities (CVEs) that have official security patches available.
PKGS-7394.how_to_solve:
1. Refresh package index: sudo apt update
2. Upgrade all packages: sudo apt upgrade -y
3. Clean up unneeded dependencies: sudo apt autoremove -y
PKGS-7394.business_impact: Unpatched vulnerabilities are the #1 entry vector for ransomware, botnets, and remote code execution exploits.
PKGS-7394.remediation_cmd: sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y && sudo apt autoremove -y
PKGS-7394.rollback_note: Individual packages can be pinned with 'apt-mark hold <pkg>'.

PKGS-7390.title: Debian/Ubuntu Package Integrity Check Tool Missing
PKGS-7390.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7390 checks for package integrity verification utilities such as debsums or rpm -V.
PKGS-7390.description: Without package integrity verification tools, system administrators cannot verify whether binaries or libraries installed on disk have been modified by rootkits or malware.
PKGS-7390.how_to_solve:
1. Install the debsums package.
2. Run a full verification of all installed packages against official repository checksums.
3. Schedule automatic weekly integrity scans.
PKGS-7390.business_impact: Inability to detect trojaned binaries or modified system executables.
PKGS-7390.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y debsums && sudo debsums -s

PKGS-7398.title: Automatic Package Updates (unattended-upgrades) Inactive
PKGS-7398.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7398 checks if unattended-upgrades or yum-cron is configured and active for automatic security patching.
PKGS-7398.description: Critical zero-day patches released by Linux vendors are not automatically applied to this system, leaving a window of exposure between vulnerability disclosure and manual patching.
PKGS-7398.how_to_solve:
1. Install unattended-upgrades package.
2. Enable automatic security updates: sudo dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades
3. Verify /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades is enabled.
PKGS-7398.business_impact: Prolonged exposure window to published exploits and automated vulnerability scanning bots.
PKGS-7398.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y unattended-upgrades && echo -e 'APT::Periodic::Update-Package-Lists "1";\nAPT::Periodic::Unattended-Upgrade "1";' | sudo tee /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades && sudo systemctl restart unattended-upgrades

PKGS-7388.title: Purged Package Configuration Residue Present
PKGS-7388.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7388 checks for removed packages whose old configuration files still reside on the filesystem in 'rc' status.
PKGS-7388.description: Unused configuration files from deleted applications remain on disk. Stale config files can lead to orphaned cron jobs or security holes.
PKGS-7388.how_to_solve:
1. Query all packages in 'rc' status: dpkg -l | grep '^rc'
2. Purge residual configuration files: sudo apt purge $(dpkg -l | awk '/^rc/ {print $2}')
PKGS-7388.business_impact: System clutter and accidental execution of orphaned service hooks.
PKGS-7388.rollback_note: Re-install package if configuration is needed.

PKGS-7387.title: Package Tooling apt-show-versions Missing
PKGS-7387.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7387 tests for apt-show-versions utility to accurately track available vs installed package versions.
PKGS-7387.description: The apt-show-versions tool enables detailed reporting of package distribution status and upgrade availability per package.
PKGS-7387.how_to_solve:
1. Install apt-show-versions package.
2. Initialize cache with apt-show-versions -i.
PKGS-7387.business_impact: Limited visibility into package version upgrade status.
PKGS-7387.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y apt-show-versions && sudo apt-show-versions -i

PKGS-7386.title: Package Manager Architecture Check
PKGS-7386.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7386 verifies enabled foreign multi-arch package architectures (e.g. i386 on amd64).
PKGS-7386.description: Multi-architecture configurations (such as 32-bit libraries on 64-bit systems) increase the attack surface by requiring additional library dependencies.
PKGS-7386.how_to_solve:
1. List foreign architectures: dpkg --print-foreign-architectures
2. If not needed, remove foreign architecture: sudo dpkg --remove-architecture i386
PKGS-7386.business_impact: Increased attack surface and unneeded library vulnerabilities.

PKGS-7384.title: Debian/Ubuntu Needrestart Tool Missing
PKGS-7384.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7384 checks for needrestart or checkrestart to detect processes running outdated in-memory libraries.
PKGS-7384.description: When security updates are applied to shared libraries (like OpenSSL or glibc), running processes continue using the vulnerable version in RAM until restarted.
PKGS-7384.how_to_solve:
1. Install needrestart.
2. Configure needrestart to automatically prompt or restart daemon services upon package upgrades.
PKGS-7384.business_impact: Vulnerabilities remain active in RAM even after disk packages have been updated.
PKGS-7384.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y needrestart && sudo needrestart -u NeedRestart::UI::stdio -r l

PKGS-7382.title: Apt-listbugs / Apt-listchanges Tool Missing
PKGS-7382.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7382 checks for tools that display release notes and critical bug notices prior to package installation.
PKGS-7382.description: Apt-listchanges shows critical security notices, deprecations, and breaking changes before package upgrades are written to disk.
PKGS-7382.how_to_solve:
1. Install apt-listchanges.
2. Configure /etc/apt/listchanges.conf to display changelog headers on upgrades.
PKGS-7382.business_impact: Risk of applying unexpected breaking changes during maintenance upgrades.

PKGS-7380.title: Package Database Consistency Errors
PKGS-7380.control_detail: Lynis Control PKGS-7380 checks the integrity of the local package manager database (dpkg/rpm).
PKGS-7380.description: Broken package dependencies or interrupted installations leave software in a half-configured, unpatched state.
PKGS-7380.how_to_solve:
1. Run 'sudo dpkg --configure -a' to finish pending setups.
2. Run 'sudo apt install -f' to resolve missing dependencies.
PKGS-7380.business_impact: Inability to apply critical security patches due to broken package database locks.

AUTH-9288.title: Direct Root Login Enabled via SSH
AUTH-9288.control_detail: Lynis Control AUTH-9288 audits SSH daemon configuration to ensure direct remote root login is disabled.
AUTH-9288.description: The master administrator account ('root') is permitted to log in directly over the internet via SSH. Automated brute-force botnets constantly target root accounts.
AUTH-9288.how_to_solve:
1. Open /etc/ssh/sshd_config in an editor.
2. Set 'PermitRootLogin no'.
3. Save file and reload SSH service: sudo systemctl restart sshd
AUTH-9288.business_impact: Severe risk of full server takeover and ransomware deployment. Violates PCI-DSS, SOC 2, and ISO 27001 compliance standards.
AUTH-9288.remediation_cmd: sudo sed -i 's/^#*PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl restart sshd
AUTH-9288.rollback_note: To revert: set 'PermitRootLogin yes' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restart sshd.

FIRE-4512.title: No Active Firewall Detected
FIRE-4512.control_detail: Lynis Control FIRE-4512 checks for the presence and active status of host-based firewall subsystems (UFW, iptables, nftables, firewalld).
FIRE-4512.description: Your server does not have an active firewall running. All network ports and internal services are directly exposed to the open network or internet.
FIRE-4512.how_to_solve:
1. Install and configure UFW or firewalld.
2. Set default incoming policy to deny and outgoing to allow.
3. Allow required ports (e.g. 22 for SSH).
4. Enable and start firewall service.
FIRE-4512.business_impact: High vulnerability to network port scanning, unauthorized remote access, and service exploitation.
FIRE-4512.remediation_cmd: sudo ufw default deny incoming && sudo ufw default allow outgoing && sudo ufw allow ssh && sudo ufw --force enable

KRNL-5830.title: Unrestricted Core Memory Dumps Enabled
KRNL-5830.control_detail: Lynis Control KRNL-5830 inspects system limits and kernel flags regarding core dump generation upon process termination.
KRNL-5830.description: When software crashes, the system writes a complete copy of its computer memory to disk. This dump can contain unencrypted user passwords, session tokens, and sensitive data.
KRNL-5830.how_to_solve:
1. Restrict core dumps in /etc/security/limits.conf (* hard core 0).
2. Set fs.suid_dumpable = 0 in /etc/sysctl.conf.
3. Reload sysctl settings.
KRNL-5830.business_impact: Sensitive data leaks if an attacker gains access to crash dump files or uses memory dump exploits.
KRNL-5830.remediation_cmd: echo '* hard core 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/security/limits.conf && sudo sysctl -w fs.suid_dumpable=0
KRNL-5830.rollback_note: Remove the '* hard core 0' entry from /etc/security/limits.conf.

SSH-7408.title: SSH Server Hardening Recommendations
SSH-7408.control_detail: Lynis Control SSH-7408 reviews SSH daemon authentication parameters, attempt throttling, and log verbosity.
SSH-7408.description: The SSH remote administration service has permissive settings (e.g. high login attempt limits or non-verbose logging) that can be tightened against automated attacks.
SSH-7408.how_to_solve:
1. In /etc/ssh/sshd_config, set MaxAuthTries 3.
2. Set LogLevel VERBOSE.
3. Restart SSH daemon: sudo systemctl restart sshd
SSH-7408.business_impact: Increased attack surface for password brute-forcing and insufficient audit trails during security incident forensics.
SSH-7408.remediation_cmd: sudo sed -i 's/^#*MaxAuthTries.*/MaxAuthTries 3/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo sed -i 's/^#*LogLevel.*/LogLevel VERBOSE/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl restart sshd
SSH-7408.rollback_note: Adjust MaxAuthTries or LogLevel in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and restart sshd.

SSH-7402.title: SSH Protocol 1 Permitted
SSH-7402.control_detail: Lynis Control SSH-7402 checks whether outdated and cryptographically broken SSH protocol version 1 is supported.
SSH-7402.description: SSHv1 contains fundamental cryptographic flaws permitting Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) session hijacking and plaintext credential extraction.
SSH-7402.business_impact: Eavesdropping and interception of administrative sessions on the local network.
SSH-7402.remediation_cmd: sudo sed -i 's/^#*Protocol.*/Protocol 2/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl restart sshd

SSH-7412.title: SSH X11 Forwarding Enabled
SSH-7412.control_detail: Lynis Control SSH-7412 verifies X11Forwarding status in sshd_config.
SSH-7412.description: X11 forwarding allows remote GUI applications to tunnel over SSH. If a remote client connects to a compromised host, the server can snoop on the client's keystrokes.
SSH-7412.how_to_solve:
1. Set 'X11Forwarding no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.
2. Restart SSH daemon.
SSH-7412.business_impact: Potential client-side credential theft and keystroke logging.
SSH-7412.remediation_cmd: sudo sed -i 's/^#*X11Forwarding.*/X11Forwarding no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl restart sshd

SSH-7414.title: SSH TCP Port Forwarding Enabled
SSH-7414.control_detail: Lynis Control SSH-7414 audits AllowTcpForwarding directive in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.
SSH-7414.description: TCP forwarding allows users to tunnel arbitrary network connections through SSH, bypassing network firewall boundary rules.
SSH-7414.how_to_solve:
1. Set 'AllowTcpForwarding no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config if tunneling is not strictly required.
2. Restart SSH daemon.
SSH-7414.business_impact: Bypassing boundary firewalls and network segmentation.
SSH-7414.remediation_cmd: sudo sed -i 's/^#*AllowTcpForwarding.*/AllowTcpForwarding no/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl restart sshd

SSH-7420.title: SSH Client Alive Interval Unconfigured
SSH-7420.control_detail: Lynis Control SSH-7420 checks ClientAliveInterval and ClientAliveCountMax timeout settings in sshd_config.
SSH-7420.description: Inactive SSH sessions remain open indefinitely, allowing unauthorized users physical access to abandoned open terminals.
SSH-7420.how_to_solve:
1. Set ClientAliveInterval 300 (5 minutes).
2. Set ClientAliveCountMax 2.
3. Restart SSH daemon.
SSH-7420.business_impact: Hijacking of unattended administrative terminal sessions.
SSH-7420.remediation_cmd: sudo sed -i 's/^#*ClientAliveInterval.*/ClientAliveInterval 300/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo sed -i 's/^#*ClientAliveCountMax.*/ClientAliveCountMax 2/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl restart sshd

AUTH-9230.title: Password Expiration and Aging Policy Missing
AUTH-9230.control_detail: Lynis Control AUTH-9230 checks password aging definitions in /etc/login.defs including PASS_MAX_DAYS and PASS_MIN_DAYS.
AUTH-9230.description: Local user passwords never expire. Stale or forgotten user accounts may retain valid credentials indefinitely.
AUTH-9230.how_to_solve:
1. Edit /etc/login.defs.
2. Set PASS_MAX_DAYS to 90.
3. Set PASS_MIN_DAYS to 1.
4. Apply to existing users: chage --maxdays 90 <user>
AUTH-9230.business_impact: Dormant account compromise; failure to meet cybersecurity insurance and data protection audit requirements.

AUTH-9204.title: Multiple User Accounts with UID 0
AUTH-9204.control_detail: Lynis Control AUTH-9204 checks for non-root user accounts configured with User ID 0 (root equivalent).
AUTH-9204.description: Only the root account should have UID 0. Additional accounts with UID 0 bypass individual audit logging, granting unauthenticated superuser privileges without audit attribution.
AUTH-9204.how_to_solve:
1. Inspect /etc/passwd for accounts where the 3rd field is '0'.
2. Change the UID of non-root accounts to a unique UID (>=1000) or delete rogue accounts.
AUTH-9204.business_impact: Severe risk of undetected administrative backdoors and complete compromise of accountability.
AUTH-9204.rollback_note: Ensure user has necessary sudo rights before changing UID.

AUTH-9218.title: User Accounts Without Password Configured
AUTH-9218.control_detail: Lynis Control AUTH-9218 inspects /etc/shadow for accounts having blank or null password hashes.
AUTH-9218.description: Accounts without a password allow any user to log in or switch user (su) without credentials, exposing the system to immediate unauthorized access.
AUTH-9218.how_to_solve:
1. Identify accounts with empty password field in /etc/shadow.
2. Lock the account (passwd -l) or set a secure password.
AUTH-9218.business_impact: Trivial unauthorized remote or local login, total system compromise.
AUTH-9218.remediation_cmd: sudo awk -F: '($2 == "" ) {print $1}' /etc/shadow | while read -r u; do sudo passwd -l "$u"; done
AUTH-9218.rollback_note: sudo passwd <user> to set a new password.

LOGG-2190.title: Linux Audit Framework (auditd) Not Running
LOGG-2190.control_detail: Lynis Control LOGG-2190 verifies the status of the Linux Auditing System (auditd) daemon and kernel event logging.
LOGG-2190.description: The Linux security audit subsystem is not active. System file changes, privilege escalation events, and unauthorized access attempts are not being recorded.
LOGG-2190.how_to_solve:
1. Install the auditd package.
2. Enable the service to start automatically at boot.
3. Start the auditd service.
LOGG-2190.business_impact: Inability to investigate security breaches, identify compromised files, or provide evidence for compliance audits.
LOGG-2190.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y auditd && sudo systemctl enable --now auditd

LOGG-2192.title: Syslog Daemon Not Active or Logging Remotely
LOGG-2192.control_detail: Lynis Control LOGG-2192 audits rsyslog / journald daemon running state and remote forwarding configuration.
LOGG-2192.description: Local log storage can be deleted or altered by an intruder who gains root access. Centralized or remote log forwarding guarantees non-repudiation.
LOGG-2192.how_to_solve:
1. Install rsyslog if missing: sudo apt install -y rsyslog
2. Enable service: sudo systemctl enable --now rsyslog
3. Configure log shipping in /etc/rsyslog.d/50-default.conf.
LOGG-2192.business_impact: Tampering with evidence during an active cyber intrusion.
LOGG-2192.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y rsyslog && sudo systemctl enable --now rsyslog

BANN-7126.title: Missing Legal Warning Login Banner
BANN-7126.control_detail: Lynis Control BANN-7126 inspects /etc/issue.net and SSH banner directives to ensure unauthorized access warnings are presented.
BANN-7126.description: The server does not display a legal warning notice before SSH login. In many jurisdictions, a warning banner is legally required to prosecute unauthorized intruders.
BANN-7126.how_to_solve:
1. Create /etc/issue.net with warning text.
2. Configure 'Banner /etc/issue.net' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.
3. Restart SSH daemon.
BANN-7126.business_impact: Weakens legal standing when prosecuting unauthorized intrusions or data theft.
BANN-7126.remediation_cmd: echo 'Authorized personnel only. All activities are monitored and recorded.' | sudo tee /etc/issue.net && sudo sed -i 's|^#*Banner.*|Banner /etc/issue.net|' /etc/ssh/sshd_config && sudo systemctl restart sshd

KRNL-5788.title: Network Kernel Security Settings Not Hardened
KRNL-5788.control_detail: Lynis Control KRNL-5788 checks sysctl network parameters for SYN flood protection, reverse path filtering, and redirect disabling.
KRNL-5788.description: The Linux network stack is using default settings that are susceptible to TCP SYN denial-of-service floods, IP packet spoofing, and rogue redirection.
KRNL-5788.how_to_solve:
1. Configure sysctl security directives in /etc/sysctl.d/99-security.conf.
2. Enable TCP syncookies and reverse path filtering.
3. Reload sysctl with 'sudo sysctl --system'.
KRNL-5788.business_impact: Vulnerability to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks and malicious traffic redirection on your local network.

KRNL-5677.title: Kernel ASLR (Address Space Layout Randomization) Inactive
KRNL-5677.control_detail: Lynis Control KRNL-5677 checks kernel.randomize_va_space sysctl value.
KRNL-5677.description: Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) randomizes memory address layouts for process execution, preventing buffer overflow and memory corruption exploits.
KRNL-5677.how_to_solve:
1. Set kernel.randomize_va_space = 2 in /etc/sysctl.d/99-security.conf.
2. Reload sysctl with sudo sysctl --system.
KRNL-5677.business_impact: Vulnerability to memory corruption and return-oriented programming (ROP) exploits.
KRNL-5677.remediation_cmd: echo 'kernel.randomize_va_space = 2' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.d/99-security.conf && sudo sysctl -w kernel.randomize_va_space=2

FILE-7524.title: Insecure Cron Job File Permissions
FILE-7524.control_detail: Lynis Control FILE-7524 examines permissions on crontab and cron directories (/etc/crontab, /etc/cron.*).
FILE-7524.description: Automated system task schedules (/etc/crontab or /etc/cron.*) have overly permissive read or write access.
FILE-7524.how_to_solve:
1. Set /etc/crontab permissions to 600.
2. Set cron directories (/etc/cron.d, /etc/cron.daily, etc.) permissions to 700.
3. Verify owner is root:root.
FILE-7524.business_impact: Low-privilege users or malware can modify scheduled tasks to gain unauthorized root administrator control.
FILE-7524.rollback_note: Re-apply default permissions if specific applications require custom cron permissions.

FILE-7532.title: Insecure Permissions on /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow
FILE-7532.control_detail: Lynis Control FILE-7532 tests file permissions and ownership on critical user identity files (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group).
FILE-7532.description: World-writable /etc/passwd or readable /etc/shadow permits unprivileged local users to create backdoor root accounts or dump password hashes.
FILE-7532.how_to_solve:
1. Set /etc/passwd permissions to 644 owned by root:root.
2. Set /etc/shadow permissions to 600 (or 640 root:shadow).
3. Set /etc/group permissions to 644.
FILE-7532.business_impact: Immediate local privilege escalation and credential compromise.
FILE-7532.remediation_cmd: sudo chmod 644 /etc/passwd /etc/group && sudo chmod 600 /etc/shadow /etc/gshadow && sudo chown root:root /etc/passwd /etc/shadow /etc/group /etc/gshadow

NAME-4404.title: No Secondary DNS Server Configured
NAME-4404.control_detail: Lynis Control NAME-4404 validates resolver configuration in /etc/resolv.conf to ensure redundant nameservers exist.
NAME-4404.description: Your system relies on a single DNS name server. If that server goes down, your server will lose internet connectivity and domain resolution.
NAME-4404.how_to_solve:
1. Add a secondary backup DNS nameserver (such as 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8) to /etc/resolv.conf or Netplan configuration.
2. Test resolution with dig or nslookup.
NAME-4404.business_impact: Risk of server downtime and service unavailability during DNS outages.
NAME-4404.rollback_note: Edit /etc/resolv.conf or Netplan config to restore previous DNS settings.

TIME-3104.title: NTP Network Time Synchronization Not Active
TIME-3104.control_detail: Lynis Control TIME-3104 checks system clock synchronization status (chrony, systemd-timesyncd, or ntpd).
TIME-3104.description: The server clock is not synchronized via Network Time Protocol (NTP). Inaccurate system clocks break SSL/TLS security certificates and corrupt log timestamps.
TIME-3104.how_to_solve:
1. Enable systemd-timesyncd or install chrony.
2. Run 'sudo timedatectl set-ntp on'.
3. Verify status with 'timedatectl status'.
TIME-3104.business_impact: Security certificate validation errors, broken authentication tokens, and unaligned security log forensic timelines.
TIME-3104.remediation_cmd: sudo timedatectl set-ntp on && sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-timesyncd

ACNT-6401.title: Dormant or Inactive User Accounts Present
ACNT-6401.control_detail: Lynis Control ACNT-6401 scans user password files and shadow database for dormant accounts with no recent login activity.
ACNT-6401.description: There are user accounts on the server that have not been logged into for over 90 days or represent former employees/services.
ACNT-6401.how_to_solve:
1. Identify unused user accounts with 'lastlog'.
2. Set default account expiration for inactive users: useradd -D -f 30
3. Lock or delete stale accounts: sudo passwd -l <user>
ACNT-6401.business_impact: Orphaned accounts are easy targets for credential reuse and unauthorized lateral movement.
ACNT-6401.remediation_cmd: sudo useradd -D -f 30 && echo 'Lock unused user: sudo passwd -l <username>'
ACNT-6401.rollback_note: To unlock a locked account: 'sudo passwd -u <username>'.

HRDN-7222.title: Compiler Available to Non-Privileged Users
HRDN-7222.control_detail: Lynis Control HRDN-7222 tests file permissions on development compilers (gcc, g++, as, clang) to prevent non-root compilation.
HRDN-7222.description: Software compilers (e.g. gcc, clang) are accessible to regular users. Attackers often use compilers on compromised servers to build local privilege escalation exploits.
HRDN-7222.how_to_solve:
1. Restrict compiler executable permissions to root only (chmod 700).
2. Alternatively, remove development packages from production servers.
HRDN-7222.business_impact: Enables attackers to compile and run zero-day exploits directly on your server.

MALW-3280.title: No Malware / Rootkit Scanner Installed
MALW-3280.control_detail: Lynis Control MALW-3280 checks for installed malware scanners, anti-virus agents, and rootkit detection utilities (rkhunter, chkrootkit, ClamAV).
MALW-3280.description: The system does not have an active malware, anti-virus, or rootkit detector (such as ClamAV or rkhunter).
MALW-3280.how_to_solve:
1. Install ClamAV and rkhunter.
2. Update malware signature databases: freshclam && rkhunter --update
3. Schedule daily scans via cron.
MALW-3280.business_impact: Hidden backdoors, cryptominers, and rootkits can operate undetected.
MALW-3280.remediation_cmd: sudo apt install -y rkhunter clamav && sudo freshclam

USB-1000.title: USB Storage Devices Not Restricted
USB-1000.control_detail: Lynis Control USB-1000 audits kernel module configuration to verify if usb-storage is blacklisted.
USB-1000.description: USB flash drives and external storage devices can be mounted without restrictions by any physical user.
USB-1000.how_to_solve:
1. Blacklist the usb-storage kernel module in /etc/modprobe.d/usb-storage.conf.
2. Reload modprobe configuration.
USB-1000.business_impact: Risk of data exfiltration or malware introduction via rogue physical USB devices.
